chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) advised me with the siwak (brushing teeth) to the extent that I feared for my teeth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of siwak in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Sunnah of the Siwak, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual purity through the divine instruction of Angel Jibraeel. The Prophet’s humorous exaggeration of fearing for his teeth highlights the exceptional frequency and thoroughness of this practice, establishing it as a highly recommended act of worship (Mustahabb) in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a reminder that minor acts of self-care, when performed with intention, carry significant spiritual weight.
